Chingy on Sidney Starr Arrested & Held with No Bond for Meeting Up with 13-Year-Old Boy (Part 3)

Part 1: https://youtu.be/tDpGD3Z34Sc
---------
Chingy sits down with Vlad to address the latest news surrounding Sidney Starr, who has reportedly been jailed without bond on charges including aggravated child molestation, sexual battery against a child under 16, and sodomy involving an alleged 13-year-old victim. The St. Louis rapper revisits the viral controversy that began after a photo at a Chicago show during his Disturbing tha Peace era, when Starr later claimed they had a relationship—an allegation Chingy has long denied.

He explains how the rumor spread through MediaTakeOut, The Breakfast Club, blogs, and social media, costing him a potential record deal and even a Chingy-branded Mastercard opportunity. Chingy also reflects on why he didn’t keep publicly fighting the claim, how he considered defamation action, and how the situation affected his career, public image, and interactions with fans. Vlad also recalls believing Chingy’s denial from the beginning.

Part 1: https://youtu.be/oJzes6G-Jac
--------
DJ Vlad sits down with Hit-Boy for a candid conversation about loyalty, family, and the risks of chasing a rap career later in life. The discussion opens with Vlad referencing his interview with Brian “Glaze” Gibbs, the Queens drug era, and the Jam Master Jay murder case, using it as a cautionary example of older street figures staying tied to dangerous situations. From there, Hit-Boy breaks down spending over $1 million—around $1.3 million by his count—on his father’s music campaign, including housing, clothes, travel, video shoots, and photo shoots.

Hit-Boy explains why he pushed the project, how the album A Game Stays With You gained attention, and why bonding with his dad and son mattered. Elliott Wilson, Master P, and 2 Chainz come up as the conversation explores father-son dynamics, age in hip-hop, and whether money can repair family trauma.

recentItems.title: Judge Mathis & Vlad Argue Over Why Rappers Get Extorted (Part 6)
recentItems.description:

Part 5: https://youtu.be/YzxOu6Saf-0
Part 1: https://youtu.be/lOCPGaKuQxw
----------
Judge Mathis and Vlad break down the complicated reality of hip-hop security, street ties, and extortion in the entertainment industry. The conversation centers on Lil Durk, OTF, THF Basu, Chicago gang culture, and why artists often keep childhood friends or “day ones” close even after fame. Vlad argues that surrounding yourself with active street figures can lead to legal trouble, while Mathis says many rappers are pressured by threats, loyalty, and a lack of trust in police protection.

The debate also covers off-duty cops, NYPD and Chicago PD security, Nation of Islam protection, Gucci Mane’s situation involving Pooh Shiesty, and Big U’s federal extortion charges tied to Los Angeles and the Rolling 60s Crips. Mathis shares his perspective from Detroit, expungement expos, and working with OGs, while weighing in on whether Durk could beat his case.

recentItems.title: Moe Gangat on Predicting Tory Lanez Will Walk Free Before He Was Found Guilty (Part 4)
recentItems.description:
Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join

Part 3: https://youtu.be/3yvMZ_9QF3M
Part 1: https://youtu.be/fjE20W3ouPQ
--------
Attorney Moe Gangat joins Vlad to revisit the Tory Lanez trial involving Megan Thee Stallion and the 2020 shooting case that ended with Daystar Peterson being found guilty. Gangat explains why he believed Lanez had a path to acquittal, pointing to the four key witnesses, the absent security guard testimony, and shifting courtroom moments involving eyewitness Sean Kelly. Vlad challenges Moe on his earlier confidence that Tory could walk free, while Moe argues the trial changed dramatically during redirect examination and that online reactions often oversimplify criminal cases. The discussion also touches on Megan’s testimony, the defense strategy, the failed appeal, Lanez’s prison stabbing, and the possibility of deportation to Canada after his sentence. A detailed legal breakdown of one of hip-hop’s most debated court cases, featuring candid analysis of evidence, witness credibility, celebrity influence, and media coverage.

recentItems.title: Charleston White: Latto Has a Bastard Baby with 21 Savage, Who's Married (Part 6)

Part 1: https://youtu.be/JfU9hp8uTqY
--------
In this VladTV interview, Charleston White addresses his viral comments about Latto and 21 Savage, explaining why he compared their situation to the backlash Clarissa Shields received over Papoose amid his divorce from Remy Ma. White argues that Black media applies different standards to women in public relationships, tying the debate to colorism, marriage, separation, and celebrity image. Vlad challenges his take by asking whether dating someone who is separated should carry the same stigma as being with a married person. The conversation also touches on Cardi B, public criticism before Shields’ Atlanta fight, 21 Savage’s response, and White’s claim that Latto’s alleged child was born out of wedlock. Later, they react to Corey Holcomb’s viral dating comments and discuss age gaps, traditional roles, and what men say they want in relationships.

---------

Chingy sits down with Vlad for a tense discussion about the 1996 Las Vegas shooting of 2Pac, revisiting the Death Row Records fallout, Suge Knight’s circle, and the long-debated role of Orlando Anderson after the Compton Foot Locker incident involving Travon Lane. Drawing from his own past around Bloods, Chingy challenges the common gang-retaliation narrative and shares why he believes Tupac was set up by forces beyond street beef, pointing to “dirty cops,” government involvement, and the deaths of people close to Pac.

The conversation also covers Biggie Smalls, the East Coast-West Coast feud, Outlawz member Yaki Kadafi’s death in New Jersey, bodyguards Frank Alexander and Michael Moore, Nevada security concerns, and the ongoing Keefe D murder case. Vlad pushes back with documented accounts while Chingy explains why key details still don’t add up to him.
